facts.text: I am trying to plan a trip to visit my mom's best friend who has been diagnosed with terminal cancer.
My ex-boyfriend texted me to inform me that his mother passed away today.
I live in New York.
I want to visit my mom's best friend in San Francisco.
I am flexible with dates but want to go as soon as possible.
I prefer to fly out of JFK or LaGuardia.
I want to spend around $500 for flights.
I want to spend $100-200 per night for accommodations.
I prefer to stay in a hotel near my mom's best friend's place.
I want recommendations for comforting books or podcasts to listen to during the trip.
I decided to book an American Airlines non-stop flight from JFK to SFO on the earliest available date.
I want to book the Hotel Zeppelin for 3 nights starting from the day I arrive.
I plan to download "The Nightingale" on my e-reader.
I plan to download "A Man Called Ove" on my e-reader.
I plan to check out "How I Built This" on my podcast app.
I plan to check out "Stuff You Should Know" on my podcast app.
I want to send a care package to my mom's best friend.
I want the care package to include a cozy blanket, a favorite book, and soothing teas.
I plan to check out Amazon and Barnes & Noble for the items I want to send.
I decided to get the Boll & Branch Soft Fleece Blanket.
I decided to include the book "When Breath Becomes Air" by Paul Kalanithi.
I am considering including a gift certificate for a massage or spa treatment in the care package.
I am thinking about sending a condolence gift or card to my ex-boyfriend even though we haven't been in touch for years.
I am still trying to process the news that my ex-boyfriend's mother passed away.
I am worried about whether sending a condolence gift or card to my ex-boyfriend would be awkward or inappropriate.
